implementation.backfill_before: _backfill_watchlist already wrapped normalize_symbol in try/except ValueError and `continue`d, so an invalid symbol was NOT copied into the watchlist, but it was skipped silently (no log). Now it logs a WARNING (message: backfill: skipping invalid rule symbol 'X' (not added to watchlist)). No behaviour change otherwise. Note backfill works per symbol, so a valid symbol on a rule with an invalid type/threshold is still backfilled.
implementation.what_is_rejected: normalize_symbol: strip+upper, must match ^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9.:_\-]{0,31}$ (so spaces, '!', empty, over 32 chars, leading '.' rejected) -> ValueError("invalid symbol"). Rule (RuleCreate): same symbol check; type must be price_above/price_below/percent_change; threshold must be > 0; window_seconds must be > 0 if given; percent_change requires window_seconds. All raise pydantic ValidationError (a ValueError). Real-PG test rows used: symbol 'bad symbol!', type 'nope', threshold -1.

implementation.commands_run: python -X faulthandler -m pytest -o faulthandler_timeout=120 (offline, and with TEST_DATABASE_URL on port 55497); initdb/pg_ctl start/stop for the throwaway cluster. No git commands that change state were run.
implementation.design_decisions: Scrub the DATABASE_URL and its parsed password from the stored/logged error text (replace with ***) instead of trusting asyncpg messages; cheap and covers invalid-DSN errors. Catch ValueError (pydantic ValidationError subclass) for bad rows rather than all Exception, so real DB/query errors still fail startup. Offline bad-rule test uses a small stub pool under the real Database (FakeDatabase holds already-validated Rule objects and cannot represent a bad row); bad watchlist symbol also tested with FakeDatabase. Empty-URL connect keeps its early return (sets last_error) rather than raising; callers decide via available. Services reads last_error via getattr so a db object without it still works.
implementation.deviations: Added last_error to tests/fakes/fake_db.py (not listed in the request but required for the offline test of the real-cause log). Rule load failure line also gained the RULES_PERSISTENCE_ENABLED=false hint (request said keep the hint; it was only on the unreachable line before). Skipped rules are logged inside Database.load_rules, so RuleStore.load is unchanged.
implementation.self_critique: Pydantic error text in the rule WARNING is multi-line and includes the input value; fine for logs but verbose. The password scrub only covers the exact URL and the parsed password string; an error echoing a percent-encoded form would not be scrubbed (asyncpg does not do that). A malformed list_rules row (API read) still raises, out of scope.
